narrative.northStar: The Sunscorched Desert Line — a printed timetable
narrative.overview: The page is a transit wayfinding sheet for a game the reader actually works: every question is a departure, every table a fares-and-times sheet, and the author the line's operator. It refuses both flanking category defaults — the dark neon gamer dashboard it replaced, and the dry wiki table it differentiates from — by owning the reader's column from a warm paper-and-ink print frame while the reading column itself stays calm and standard. Flatness is law: sun-bleached paper ground, warm press ink, hairline rules, one ochre-gold line accent. Depth comes from rule weight, never from gradients, blurs, or halos.
keyCharacteristics: Timetable frame, standard reading column — the world owns masthead, rules, tables, and openers only.
Flat press color only; one accent plus four functional mineral keys.
Heavy-thin double rules above every stop; hairline ruled fares sheet.
Value-by-mark: stop-tabs, room flags, glyph marks, and exactly two reserved ink inversions.
No JavaScript, no build step; Atkinson Hyperlegible body and strong contrast are binding.

rules.name: The One Reserve Rule
rules.body: A full ink inversion (paper text on Press Ink) is reserved for the row the reader came for — used at most twice on the whole page. Rarity is the point; anything more makes it wallpaper.

rules.name: The Mark-Before-Hue Rule
rules.body: Importance and state are drawn as marks first — gold stop-tabs, square note flags, geometric event glyphs — and the mineral color-coding rides on those marks. Never replace a mark with a hue field (and the side-stripe-on-content pattern is refused).

rules.name: The Flat-Press Rule
rules.body: Every fill is flat. No gradients of any kind, no blur or glass, no offset block shadows. Depth is rule weight: whisper hairlines for texture, 1px for row rules, 2-3px Press Ink for structure.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Two faces, two jobs, never swapped: condensed caps own the frame; Atkinson owns every sentence. Numbers in data columns set tabular-nums.

dos: Do keep every fill flat and every rule in the four weights (whisper / hairline / 2px / 3px ink); depth is rules, not effects.
Do set the four setups apart with the mineral keys — at AA contrast (>=4.5:1 as text) as dots, tabs, and route-name text, never as fields behind text.
Do reserve the full ink inversion for a single arrival row per table family, and set all data numerals tabular.
Do theme the browser chrome from the palette: selection (Signal Gold on ink), focus (2px solid Gold-Deep, 3px offset), thin dust scrollbars, gold summary markers.
Do open every numbered stop with the 3px+1px double rule and a gold stop-code chip; unnumbered interludes never carry codes.
donts: Don't use any gradient, glass/blur, glow, or hard offset shadow — zero-gradient is a standing brief commitment, and the flat-press world is the enforcement.
Don't put colored side-stripes on content (cards, notes, list items): marks precede stripes; if a mark earns its place, draw the flag square instead.
Don't touch the author's first-person copy, the desert-marker convention, or any wiki-traced number without re-checking pinned revisions.
Don't introduce JavaScript, a build step, or new dependencies — plain HTML + one CSS file is the confirmed constraint.

Don't add eyebrows/kickers over headings; the masthead running head (the bordered schedule bar under the sticky bar) is the one sanctioned two-part opener, because it carries real departure information.
